item.description: First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, in partnership with Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division, Justin Page, Harry T. Chavis, Jr., Special Agent in Charge of the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, and Brendan Cox, Chief of Police of the Albany Police Department, announced federal charges against fifteen alleged members and associates of the Untouchable Gorilla Stone Nation (“UGSN”). Illegal Aliens Sentenced For Scheme To Make And Cash Fraudulent Payroll Checks
item.description:
MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that two foreign nationals unlawfully present in Oklahoma were sentenced on charges relating to a fraudulent payroll check scheme.  
  • Bairon Nayn Cabrera-Martinez, 36, an illegal alien from Honduras unlawfully present in LeFlore County, Oklahoma, was sentenced to a term of 33 months in prison for one count of Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud, and 33 months in prison for one count of Unlawful Reentry of Removed Alien.  The court set the terms to be served concurrently.  On April 1, 2026, Cabrera-Martinez pleaded guilty to the charges in federal district court. 
  • Carlos Eduardo Nuila-Ramos, 36, an illegal alien from El Salvador unlawfully present in LeFlore County, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 22 months in prison for one count of Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud and 22 months in prison for one count of Unlawful Reentry of Removed Alien.  The court set the terms to be served concurrently. On May 20, 2026, Nuila-Ramos pleaded guilty to the charges in federal district court.  
  • The court also ordered the defendants to pay restitution in the amount of $299,474.00.
On July 17, 2026, co-defendant Carlos Banegas-Contreras, 47, an illegal alien from Honduras, was sentenced to 27 months in prison for one count of Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud after entering a guilty plea to the charge on October 6, 2025.According to investigators, in June of 2023, Cabrera-Martinez, Nuila-Ramos, Banegas-Contreras, and others conspired to use fake identification cards to cash 178 fraudulent paychecks totaling $299,474.00 at three check-cashing businesses and five branches of a local bank.  The fraudulent paychecks were designed to look like they had been issued by a building materials supply company in the Eastern District of Oklahoma.

item.title: Afghan citizen pleads guilty to, sentenced for Visa fraud
item.description: U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Dilbar Gul Dilbar a/k/a Dilbar Gul Taj Ali Khan, a citizen of Afghanistan, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Frank P. Geraci, Jr. to Visa fraud. He was then sentenced to serve six months in prison.

item.title: Adair County Resident Sentenced For Illegally Possessing Firearm
item.description: MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Jeremy Lee Poafpybitty, age 41, of Bunch, Oklahoma, was sentenced to 57 months in prison for one count of Felon in Possession of a Firearm.On November 3, 2025, Poafpybitty pleaded guilty to the charge.  According to investigators, on May 6, 2025, law enforcement discovered Poafpybitty in possession of a 9mm semi-automatic pistol after having been previously convicted of a crime punishable by more than one year imprisonment.

item.title: Seneca Falls man arrested, charged with production and possession of child pornography
item.description: U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Bradley R. Orlopp, 38, of Seneca Falls, NY, was arrested and charged by criminal complaint with the production and possession of child pornography. Because of a prior conviction involving the sexual abuse of a minor, the charges carry a minimum of 25 years in prison, a maximum of 50 years, a lifetime period of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine.

item.title: Orleans Parish Resident Sentenced for Violating the Controlled Substances Act and Gun Control Act
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LA – DIONTE DORSEY, (“DORSEY”), age 45, of New Orleans, was sentenced to 48 months imprisonment, followed by five (5) years of supervised release, by the U.S. District Judge Carl J. Barbier on September 24, 2026, announced U.S. Attorney David I Courcelle. DORSEY had previously pled guilty to Counts 1, 4, and 8 of the indictment pending against him. DORSEY was also ordered to pay a $300 mandatory special assessment fee.

item.title: Billings man sentenced to more than 14 years in prison for trafficking meth as part of drug ring
item.description: A Billings man who was part of a large-scale drug ring operating out of Mexico that trafficked significant amounts of methamphetamine into Montana was sentenced today to 14 years and two months in prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release.

item.title: Former Ada Resident Sentenced For Involuntary Manslaughter
item.description: MUSKOGEE, OKLAHOMA – The United States Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma announced that Heather Lynn Harjo, age 40, formerly of Ada, Oklahoma, was sentenced to thirty-seven months in prison for one count of Involuntary Manslaughter in Indian Country.On October 17, 2026, Harjo pleaded guilty to the charge.  According to investigators, on April 28, 2025, while visiting an Ada residence, Harjo became involved in an altercation and—unreasonably believing herself to be in danger of imminent death or serious bodily injury—pulled a 9mm pistol and fired a single shot, striking and killing the victim.  Harjo fled and was captured eight weeks later on a fugitive arrest warrant in Dallas, Texas.
